       PUBLIC HEARINGS

       4.1     BYLAW NO. 2063

               The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2063 at 5:33pm.

                                                  MiriUtfes of the Regular CQunGll iyieetirjg - May IS, 2022




Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Rachael Sansom of Grayland
Consulting Ud. has applied on iaehalfof Sheldrake Gonstruetion Ltd and Phyllis & Doriald
Griffiths to amend the zoning of 2869> 2875, 2885 Leigh Road and 1080 Dunford Avenue
from the R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential) Zone to the CCl (City Centre) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a six-storey mixed-use
building containing approximately 78 residential units and 870 m2 of commercial space.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1.   The following contributions as a bonus for increased density:


a. $750 per SFE towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;
b. $2,850 per SFE towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and
c. $10.75 per m2 of commercial gross floor area.


2. That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan, as Well as a
construction parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000
standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a
Building Permit;

3. That the developer will connect and be responsible for any upgrades required to the
services and utilities required for the development;


4. That the developer will install tree protection fencing around City boulevard trees to
the satisfaction of the Parks Manager, prior to any land alteration;


5. That the building be strata titled into individual residential units prior to the
issuance of an occupancy permit, to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer;


6. That the developer consolidate the parcels in accordance with the CCl zone
regulations, prior to the issuance of a development permit;


7. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the
proposed residential building(s) that ensures parking is allocated to each unit and
visitors as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in exchange for
compensation separate from that of a residential unit; and


8. That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall
feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 chargi ng or higher to the
parking space; and


1. Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging;
2. Where an electric vehicle energy management system is implemented (load
sharing), a qualified professional may specify a minimum performance standard to





      ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and
      3. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing Equipment (EVSE) in
      operation and the Strata Council may not prevent an owner, occupant, or tenant from
      installing the EVcharging equipment.


      9. That a separate covenant be registered that informs individuals about the potential
      noise and nuisance that may be generated by neighbouring business park uses.

      Council has also, by resolution, requested that the applicant discuss the opportunity to
      incorporate units for the Attainable Home Ownership Program with staff prior to Public
      Hearing.
      Since Council finalized their policy amendment for the Attainable Home Ownership
      Program making participating in the Program mandatory for new applications after this
      resolution was made, they may wish to exempt the applicant from being required to
      participate. The applicant may voluntarily opt into participating in the program at the
      time of development permit. Should Council wish to make participating in the Program
      mandatory for this project, they may wish to pass a resolution to that effect during
      consideration of 2nd and 3rd readings of Bylaw No. 2063.
      This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.

      Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

      Rachael Sansom, Grayland Consulting Ltd., gave a presentation on the proposed
      development, noting the location plan, project components, and project design.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      Mayor Young called for a third and final time for presentations.

      M. Wagner. #104-2669 Deville Rd. expressed support for the proportion of public
      amenity but expressed concerns about potential impacts to trees.

      K. Clark. 2878 Leigh Rd. posed questions about potential impacts to traffic.

      E. Holler. 2898 Maurice Ln. expressed concerns about potential impacts to parking
      spaces.

      Mike. 953 Glen Willow PI. expressed support for the proposal.

      C. Bovd. 967 Whirlawav PI. expressed support for the proposal.

      S. Boivin. 2890 Leigh Rd. expressed concerns about potential impacts to trees, traffic,
      and the lack of proposed 3-bedroom units.

      Mayor Young declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2063 closed at 5:52 pm.

4.3   BYLAW NO. 2045

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No, 2045 at 6:01pnri>

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Rachael Sansom of Grayland
      Consulting Ltd. has applied on behalf of 1080581 BC Ltd. to amend the zoning of 2615
      Sooke Road from the R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential) Zone to the C9 (Community
      Town Centre Pedestrian 9) Zone.

      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a mixed-use building
      containing approximately 115 residential units and two ground level commercial units
      that face Sooke Road.

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

      1; The following contributions as a bonus for increased density;

      a. $2,074 per SFE towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and
      b. $610 per SFEtowards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund

      2. That frontage improvements, a stormwater rnanagement plan, as well as a
      construction parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000
      standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a
      Building Permit;
      3. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the
      proposed residential building that ensures parking is allocated to each unit and visitors

            as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in exchange for compensation
            separate from that of a residential unit;

            4. That no occupancy permit be issued for the proposed building unless a strata plan
            for the building has been registered, to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer;

            5. That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall
            feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to the
            parking space, and that:

            a. Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging;
            b. Where an electric vehicle management system is implemented (load sharing), a
            qualified professional may specify a minimum performance standard to ensure a
            sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging and;
            c. The owner/tenant is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing Equipment
            (EVSE) in operation and the Strata Council/Landlord may not prevent an owner,
            occupant or tenant from installing the EVcharging equipment.

            6. That a road dedication plan is registered to the satisfaction of the Director of
            Engineering and the Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure

            Council also has, by resolution, authorized the Director of Planning to issue a variance
            within the Form and Character Development Permit to allow the applicant to utilize the
            City Centre parking ratio for the project.

            This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood Centre
            designation.

            Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
            Government Act.

            Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

            Rachael Sansom, Grayland Consulting Ltd., gave a presentation on the proposed project,
            providing information on the site location, neighbourhood consultation process, and
            project components.

            Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

            Mayor Young called for a third and final time for presentations. There being none, he
            declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2045 closed at 6:08pm.
